risks.note: Operations depend on the availability and pricing of aluminium, ferro alloys and other critical raw materials. Fluctuations in commodity prices, energy costs or supply shortages may affect production costs, profitability and working capital requirements - a structural exposure for a secondary-aluminium converter where cost of goods sold runs well above 80% of net sales.

Uncertainties from geopolitical conflicts, changing trade policies, inflationary pressures and global economic slowdowns may impact demand, international trade flows, logistics and customer spending across key markets. Also flagged separately among the MD&A 'Threats' as economic slowdown and geopolitical uncertainties.

The Company is exposed to foreign exchange fluctuations through imports of raw materials and export transactions. Significant exchange-rate movements may impact procurement costs, export competitiveness and overall financial performance. Structural, given Consolidated Gross Export Sales of Rs 9,834 Lakhs in FY 2025-26.

The metal industry faces intense competition from domestic and international manufacturers. Sustained pricing pressure and evolving customer expectations require continuous improvement in product quality, operational efficiency, innovation and cost optimisation.

The Company operates in a highly regulated environment. Changes in environmental regulations, taxation policies, trade regulations, product standards and corporate governance requirements may necessitate additional investments and operational adjustments.

Disruptions in procurement, transportation, port operations or supplier performance may impact the timely availability of raw materials and execution of customer orders; the Company is strengthening its sourcing strategy and supply chain resilience.

The Company operates solely in the business of manufacturing and trading of ferrous and non-ferrous metals with no other reportable segments, and Aluminium Wire Rod, Aluminium Deox and Conductors & Cables were the key contributors to performance in FY 2025-26 - leaving results concentrated on the aluminium value chain and on steel and power end-markets.

Long-term success depends on attracting, developing and retaining a skilled workforce; talent availability, employee engagement, succession planning and workplace safety remain key priorities in supporting business growth.

currentContext.expansion: Arfin's expansion is organised around its Gujarat manufacturing cluster and a staged history of capacity additions. The main hub at Chhatral (near Ahmedabad) comprises a cluster of four integrated production units for Aluminium Wire Rod, Aluminium Deox, Ferro Alloys and Cored Wire, with a separate facility at the same location dedicated to Conductors; a Dhanot Village plant produces Aluminium Deox and Aluminium Secondary Ingots about 2 km away, and a Vadaswami Village plant produces Aluminium Cubes and Aluminium Notch Bars about 5 km away. A Raigad (Maharashtra) branch office supports steel-sector customers. The disclosed growth milestones run: manufacture of Al Wire Rod and Al De-Ox started with annual capacity of 15,000 MT and 20,000 MT; entry to the ferrous and non-ferrous metals business after surrendering the NBFC licence in 2012; a Ferro Alloy plant of 1,200 MT; BSE listing together with a cored wire plant of 2,400 MT annual capacity; a new Ingot plant of 6,000 MT; capacity expansion of the cored wire and ferro alloy plants; a Conductor & Cable plant with installed capacity of 12,000 MT; a second Ingot plant of 12,000 MT; the JFE Shoji (Japan) strategic partnership; NSE listing and incorporation of wholly owned subsidiary Arfin Titanium & Speciality Alloys Ltd; and expansion of the product portfolio with Inoculants and AL-59 Conductors. Total installed annual production capacity stands at 71,000 metric tons. Looking forward, the Medium Voltage Covered Conductors (MVCC) project is described as an important upcoming initiative which, upon commissioning, is expected to expand product offerings and strengthen the Company's position in the power transmission industry; ATSAL, the wholly owned subsidiary, is being built out around high-value speciality alloy products. A 1200 KW solar power plant was installed at Terwada village, Banaskantha in 2022 for captive energy use. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed anywhere in these bundles. (The MVCC, ATSAL and solar details, and the Vadaswami plant description, sit in the profile/MD-message bundle of the same annual report - the capex bundle is truncated mid-sentence at the Vadaswami plant.)
